narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist Luke; measured, orderly storytelling.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: Jesus of Nazareth, about thirty; calm authority, teaching in parables, warning and consoling.

ruler-of-the-synagogue.name: Ruler of the synagogue
ruler-of-the-synagogue.note: Head of the synagogue where the bent woman is healed; indignant, lecturing the people rather than facing Jesus.

a-man-in-the-crowd.name: A certain man
a-man-in-the-crowd.note: Unnamed man on the road to Jerusalem asking whether few are saved; curious, respectful.

pharisees.name: Pharisees
pharisees.note: Some Pharisees warning Jesus that Herod means to kill him; urgent, perhaps feigned concern.

1.t: And there were present, at that very time, some that told him of the Galileans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.

2.t: And he answering, said to them:
Think you that these Galileans were sinners above all the men of Galilee, because they suffered such things?

3.t: No, I say to you: but unless you shall do penance, you shall all likewise perish.

4.t: Or those eighteen upon whom the tower fell in Siloe and slew them: think you that they also were debtors above all the men that dwelt in Jerusalem?

5.t: No, I say to you: but except you do penance, you shall all likewise perish.

6.t: A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard: and he came seeking fruit on it and found none.

7.t: And he said to the dresser of the vineyard: Behold, for these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree and I find none. Cut it down therefore. Why cumbereth it the ground?

8.t: But he answering, said to him: Lord, let it alone this year also, until I dig about it and dung it.

9.t: And if happily it bear fruit: but if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.

10.t: And he was teaching in their synagogue on their sabbath.

11.t: And behold there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years. And she was bowed together: neither could she look upwards at all.

12.t: Whom when Jesus saw, he called her unto him and said to her:
Woman, thou art delivered from thy infirmity.

13.t: And he laid his hands upon her: and immediately she was made straight and glorified God.

14.t: And the ruler of the synagogue being angry that Jesus had healed on the sabbath answering, said to the multitude:
Six days there are wherein you ought to work. In them therefore come and be healed: and not on the sabbath day.

15.t: And the Lord answering him, said:
Ye hypocrites, doth not every one of you, on the sabbath day, loose his ox or his ass from the manger and lead them to water?

16.t: And ought not this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?

17.t: And when he said these things, all his adversaries were ashamed: and all the people rejoiced for all the things that were gloriously done by him.

18.t: To what is the kingdom of God like, and whereunto shall I resemble it?

19.t: It is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and cast into his garden: and it grew and became a great tree, and the birds of the air lodged in the branches thereof.

20.t: Whereunto shall I esteem the kingdom of God to be like?

21.t: It is like to leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.

22.t: And he went through the cities and towns teaching and making his journey to Jerusalem.

23.t: And a certain man said to him:
Lord, are they few that are saved?

24.t: Strive to enter by the narrow gate: for many, I say to you, shall seek to enter and shall not be able.

25.t: But when the master of the house shall be gone in and shall shut the door, you shall begin to stand without; and knock at the door, saying: Lord, open to us. And he answering, shall say to you: I know you not, whence you are.

26.t: Then you shall begin to say: We have eaten and drunk in thy presence: and thou hast taught in our streets.

27.t: And he shall say to you: I know you not, whence you are. Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.

28.t: There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth; when you shall see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God: and you yourselves thrust out.

29.t: And there shall come from the east and the west and the north and the south: and shall sit down in the kingdom of God.

30.t: And behold, they are last that shall be first: and they are first that shall be last.

31.t: The same day, there came some of the Pharisees, saying to him:
Depart, and get thee hence, for Herod hath a mind to kill thee.

32.t: Go and tell that fox: Behold, I cast out devils and do cures, to-day and to-morrow, and the third day I am consummated.

33.t: Nevertheless, I must walk to-day and to-morrow and the day following, because it cannot be that a prophet perish, out of Jerusalem.

34.t: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that killest the prophets; and stonest them that are sent to thee, how often would I have gathered thy children as the bird doth her brood under her wings, and thou wouldest not?

35.t: Behold your house shall be left to you desolate. And I say to you that you shall not see me till the time come when you shall say: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
